column1: 큰물이 오기 전, 어머니가 연이의 버선을 꿰맸다.
column2: Before the flood came, Mother was mending Yeoni's socks.
“That thread is so much bluer than the rest.”
“So Yeoni's socks can be found at a glance.
The last knot is Sobok's to tie.”

column1: 그날 저녁, 둑 너머로 물이 넘었다.
column2: That evening, the water came over the embankment.
There was only one boat.
“I'm coming with you.”
“You stay with Dano and keep the lamp lit at home.
So the children can find their way.”
Mother lifted a small child into the boat.

column1: 배 안에는 관아 낙인이 찍힌 쌀자루가 있었다.
column2: In the boat were rice sacks branded with the magistrate's office seal.
A night with the lamp oil running low.
“Do you think Mother can see this light?”
“Don't shut the door.
So anyone can come in.”
Three days later, they found Mother downstream.

column1: 그날 배에 누가 탔는지는 끝내 몰랐다.
column2: No one ever learned who was on the boat that day.
“Sister, I couldn't borrow any rice today either.”
“They say the magistrate's office is handing out rice.
Our names are in the register, after all.”

column1: 그날 저녁, 이서는 하나 남은 죽을 두 그릇에 반씩 나눠 담았다.
column2: That evening, Iseo split the last of the porridge into two bowls.

column1: 단오가 자기 그릇을 이서 쪽으로 밀었다.
column2: Dano pushed his bowl toward her.
“You eat first.

column1: 나는 낮에 나루에서 감자 하나 얻어먹었어.”
column2: Someone gave me a potato at the ferry today.”
“I can tell when you're lying.
Half each.

column1: 내일 쌀 받으면 그때 더 먹자.”
column2: We'll eat more tomorrow when we get the rice.”
Twenty days later, the relief station.

column1: 담벼락의 소복은 줄이 끝날 때까지 다가오지 않았다.
column2: Sobok, by the wall, didn't come closer until the line had ended.
Part One · Choice 1 / 5
Behind the Relief Station
Clerk
Iseo's turn.
The clerk turned the register around to show her.
“Your name isn't on this year's page.
Someone scraped it off with a knife.”
“If water had soaked it, the whole page would be stained.
Only my line was scraped.”

column1: 빈 바가지를 든 이서를 담 모퉁이의 작은 손이 불렀다.
column2: As Iseo stood with her empty gourd, a small hand beckoned her from the corner of the wall.
It was Sobok.

column1: “장례 다음 날, 연이가 이 자루 옆에 있었어요.
column2: “The day after the funeral, Yeoni was right here by these sacks.
The magistrate's office says she drowned.”

column1: 담 뒤의 소복, 해 지면 떠나는 사공, 오늘 여천을 뜨는 박 유모.
column2: Sobok behind the wall, the boatwoman who leaves at sundown, Nanny Park who leaves Yeocheon today.
Who should she go to before the sun sets?
Search the river with Sobok
Follow the boatwoman
Stop the nanny before she leaves

The Sock Downstream
Sobok fished a sock out from between the rocks.

column1: 뒤축의 파란 실, 끝에 소복이 지은 매듭.
column2: Blue thread at the heel, and at the end, the knot Sobok had tied.
“That's my knot.
It's the last pair Yeoni wore.
Ask how it got all the way down here.”

column1: 소복은 버선을 뒤집어 푸른 실이 풀리지 않도록 손에 감았다.
column2: Sobok turned the sock inside out and wound the blue thread around her hand so it wouldn't unravel.

column1: “관아에서 제 말을 안 믿어도, 이 매듭을 보면 어디서 찾았는지 설명할 수 있어요.”
column2: “Even if the magistrate's office won't believe me, with this knot I can show where I found it.”

column1: “연이가 죽었다고 누가 확인했는지 백문재 어른에게 묻자.
column2: “Let's ask Master Baek Munjae who confirmed that Yeoni died.
You keep the sock.”
The sock alone can't tell when Yeoni got off the boat.

column1: 소복은 찾은 자리와 날짜부터 적어 달라 했다.
column2: Sobok asked them to write down where and when she found it first.
Part One · Choice 2 / 5
The Night of Writing Names
Baek Munjae
The woman who gave them shelter

column1: 이서와 소복은 백문재의 집 앞에서 문이 열릴 때까지 기다렸다.
column2: Iseo and Sobok waited outside Baek Munjae's house until the door opened.

column1: 문재가 이들을 알아보고 먼저 안으로 들인다.
column2: Munjae recognizes them and lets them in before they can speak.
“Don't talk about the death roll outside my door.

column1: 네가 무엇을 보고 왔는지 안에서 들려다오.”
column2: Come inside and tell me what you've seen.”

column1: 이서가 먼저 만난 사람이 남긴 단서를 들고 백문재의 집에 왔다.
column2: Iseo came to Baek Munjae's house carrying the clue left by the first person she met.
The woman who took Sobok in stepped over the threshold too.
“You and your brother are both on the death roll.
And the date of death is the same.
Nothing says anyone saw a body.”
“Writing down that Sobok is alive is fine.

column1: 주소까지 쓰면 아전들이 우리 집부터 두드리겠죠.”
column2: But write the address too, and the clerks will be knocking on my door first.”
Munjae put down his brush.

column1: 주소를 적을 칸도 아직 비어 있었다.
column2: The space for the address was still blank.
“Please write down the date Sobok was alive first.

column1: 집 주소는 저하고 먼저 이야기하시면 안 될까요?”
column2: Could you talk to me before writing the address?”
Bring Sobok's name back, and an investigation begins.

column1: 보관하면 거처는 지키지만 소복은 계속 죽은 아이다.
column2: Keep it hidden, and her shelter is safe, but on paper she stays a dead child.
How much of Sobok's name should go on record today?
Record her name, if Sobok wants it
Keep the name hidden for now
The Name Kept Indoors

column1: 여인이 문을 지키는 동안 이서는 소복의 말을 봉투에 넣었다.
column2: While the woman watched the door, Iseo sealed Sobok's statement in an envelope.
The clerk's footsteps fade away.

column1: “네가 들어가는 날까지 이 종이는 내가 가지고 있을게.”
column2: “I'll keep this paper until the day you go in.”

column1: “그럼 동생을 찾는 동안 다른 아이들이 어디서 기다릴지도 정해야 해요.
column2: “Then while we look for my sister, we have to decide where the other children will wait.
The barn door doesn't lock.”

column1: 진술을 봉하자 여인은 이모 집에 남을 수 있었다.
column2: With the statement sealed, the woman could stay at her aunt's house.

column1: 헛간 아이들은 오늘 밤 잘 곳이 필요했다.
column2: The children in the barn needed somewhere to sleep tonight.
Part One · Choice 3 / 5
Coins in the Barn
Okrye
Iseo found Okrye at the ferry landing.

column1: 소복 이야기를 듣자 옥례가 선착장 뒤 헛간을 가리켰다.
column2: When she heard about Sobok, Okrye pointed to the barn behind the dock.

column1: “눈에 띄지 않게 오늘 밤 묵을 곳을 구할 수 있어요?”
column2: “Can you find a place for them tonight without anyone noticing?”
“Let's go to the ferry barn first.

column1: 아직 남은 아이가 몇인지 보아야 방을 구할 수 있어.”
column2: I need to see how many children are left before I can find rooms.”
There were children on the straw in the barn.

column1: 아전들이 나루를 돌고 있어 해 지기 전에 옮겨야 했다.
column2: Clerks were making rounds of the landing, so they had to be moved before sundown.
“This money came from the Jeong family.

column1: 뱃삯을 다 대는 대신 아이들 머문 곳을 먼저 알려 달래.”
column2: They'll pay every fare, but they want to be told first where the children are staying.”

column1: 주머니가 열려 있는 동안, 헛간의 아이들은 한 명씩 자기 짐을 묶었다.
column2: While the purse lay open, the children in the barn tied up their bundles one by one.

column1: “우리한테는 아직 그 집이 왜 그걸 알아야 하는지 설명해 준 사람이 없어요.”
column2: “No one has told us yet why that family needs to know.”

column1: 정씨 집이면 오늘 밤 다 옮긴다.
column2: With the Jeong family, everyone moves tonight.

column1: 나루 사람들과 나누면 늦지만 집마다 따로 맡는다.
column2: Sharing with the ferry folk is slower, but each household takes a child separately.

column1: 아이들이 오늘 밤 잘 곳을 어떻게 마련할까?
column2: How should they find the children a place to sleep tonight?
Accept one family's backing
Share the cost among many households
A Night Shared Out

column1: 나루 사람들이 아이들을 저마다 집으로 데려갔다.

Okrye spreads out a quilt for the child who's left.
